e.etymology: In the United States mostly a spelling of Vada or Vayda, a name of uncertain origin known from the 1991 film My Girl. Vaida is also a Lithuanian name, the feminine of Vaidas.
The Norwegian form of Danish Esben, from Old Norse Asbjorn, god plus bear. Espen Askeladd, the Ash Lad, is the hero of Norwegian folk tales.
e.note: Easily heard as Aspen, and on paper it can be misread as ESPN.

e.etymology: An old Germanic name from adal, noble, and lind, soft or gentle, the source of Adelina and Adeline. It was revived by the character Adalind Schade in the TV series Grimm.
A spelling of Adonis, the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite in Greek myth. The name comes from the Phoenician adon, lord.

assoc.t: an Adonis, a strikingly handsome man

e.etymology: A respelling of Ivy, the climbing evergreen plant, from Old English ifig.
From Hebrew Pinechas, the name of Aaron's zealous grandson. It probably comes from Egyptian pa-nehesy, the Nubian; an old Hebrew reading takes it as oracle. Phineas is the usual English form.
A spelling of Anvi, a modern Indian girls' name given as a name of a goddess. Its Sanskrit root is not established.
A Haitian form of Marvin, with the -ens ending found in Haitian names such as Rubens and Lovens. Marvin goes back to the Welsh name Merfyn.
A respelling of Alani, the Hawaiian word for the orange tree and its fruit.
A Brazilian name built on Eder with the English-style -son ending, in the pattern of Anderson and Emerson, which are common first names in Brazil.
A modern coinage that joins the Zay- sound of Zayla and Zayden to the -lani ending of Leilani and Kailani.
From Greek Berenike, the Macedonian form of Pherenike, from pherein, to bring, and nike, victory. Several queens of Ptolemaic Egypt bore it; Bernice and Veronica are later forms of the same name.
From Old Norse Sigridr, from sigr, victory, and fridr, beautiful. It appears in the Norse sagas and has been borne by Scandinavian royalty.
An American coinage of the 1990s, built on the Tav- of Tavon and Tavares with the -ion ending of Davion and Javion.
From Greek kalliste, most beautiful, the superlative of kalos. It is close kin to Callisto, the huntress of Greek myth, and to the Latin name Callistus.
namesakes: Callista Gingrich (US ambassador and wife of Newt Gingrich)

e.etymology: From Irish niamh, brightness or lustre. In Irish myth Niamh is the daughter of the sea god Manannan who leads the poet Oisin to Tir na nOg, the land of eternal youth.
e.note: The Irish spelling is said NEEV; most Americans will need to be told how to say or spell it.

e.etymology: In Greek mythology Triton is a sea god, the merman son of Poseidon and Amphitrite. Neptune's largest moon is named for him.

assoc.t: King Triton, Ariel's father in The Little Mermaid

e.etymology: An English surname, son of Wood, where Wood was a name for someone who lived or worked in a forest. It was used as a first name in the 19th-century United States.
From the town of Melrose in the Scottish Borders, named with Gaelic maol, bare, and ros, headland. It became a surname and then a given name.
From Hebrew Elimelekh, my God is king. In the Book of Ruth Elimelech is Naomi's husband; the name is also given in honor of the Hasidic master Elimelech of Lizhensk.

A Slavic form of John, written Jan in Polish and Czech, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious. Yan is also a Chinese given name written with several different characters, and a Brazilian spelling of Ian.
In the US mostly the English word atom, from Greek atomos, indivisible. Atom is also an old Armenian male name, borne by filmmaker Atom Egoyan.

assoc.t: atom, the basic unit of matter

e.etymology: A surname used as a first name, almost always in honor of New York Yankees shortstop Derek Jeter.

assoc.t: Derek Jeter, New York Yankees shortstop

e.meaning: little bear; pet form of Mikhail
e.etymology: A Russian pet form of Misha, itself short for Mikhail (Michael). Mishka is also the everyday Russian word for a bear cub or teddy bear. In the US it is given mostly to girls.
A respelling of Sage, which is both the fragrant herb and the word for a wise person, each reaching English from Latin through Old French.
A short form of Mariah, Zariah and other names ending in -riah, used on its own.
From Sanskrit ojas, bodily strength and vitality. In Ayurveda ojas is the essence that sustains life and health.
Invented by George R. R. Martin for Renly Baratheon in A Song of Ice and Fire. It came into use for babies after the TV series Game of Thrones.

assoc.t: Renly Baratheon in Game of Thrones

e.etymology: A modern coinage that swaps the first letter of Dylan or Rylan for a Z.
